Subject: Post-call: Searchlytics embedding fit & next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope for a short model-fit evaluation.

Recap (what we heard)
- Objective: improve site search & support KB retrieval for Searchlytics’ public docs + internal support transcripts (hybrid content: long manuals, short FAQs, conversational logs).
- Size & shape: ~1.2M docs total; initial eval slice: 1,000 sample docs + 10k query set (you confirmed you can share a de-identified sample).
- Success metrics: semantic search precision@10, mean reciprocal rank (MRR), and recall@100 for recall-sensitive flows.
- Constraints: must pass PII redaction before leaving their environment; acceptable model latency <30ms per embed on batch hardware target.

What we propose from Redwood
1) Run a 1k-sample embedding comparison across three candidate model families and produce a short dashboard with MAP@10, MRR and cosine-sim drift baseline. Candidates: open-embed-4-large (dense, 3k dim), redwood-embed-compact-8bit (quantized, 768 dim), and sbert-distil-v2 (lightweight baseline).
2) Provide prompt/embedding sets, evaluation notebook and a candidate index sample (JSONL) so you can sanity-check locally.
3) Flag drift & dimensionality considerations: if compact 768-dim meets recall targets we recommend it for cost-sensitive production; otherwise use the larger dense model with caching and hybrid reranking.

Ask from you
- Share the 1k de-identified sample and a representative query list (we discussed anonymized support queries and a document parity list).
- Any hard constraints on model licensing/allowed OSS families?

Next steps & owners
- Ellen / Rajiv: share sample files (deadline: Wed EOD PT).
- Redwood (Ben + Marissa): run evaluation and deliver results + a decision recommendation (target: Fri end of week).

I attached a short evaluation checklist (see later message) and will follow up with a HubSpot record and a shared Drive folder.

—

Ben / team — quick technical update from the eval pass. I attached a short PDF with the initial quality report (semantic_quality_report_q1.pdf). Highlights:

- Topline: on the 1k sample, redwood/open-embed-4-large outperforms the compact 768-8bit model on MAP@10 (0.52 vs 0.41) and MRR (0.57 vs 0.44). Distil baseline sits at 0.35 MAP@10.
- Latency: compact-768 (quantized) hits median 12ms embed, 95th 28ms on our test profile; open-embed-4-large median 38ms (95th 120ms) — so open-embed needs caching + batching to meet latency SLOs.
- Dimensionality: 768-dim indexes are ~40% smaller on disk and show small degradation for short queries; long-context documents favor higher dimensional vectors for recall.
- Drift note: we computed cosine-sim population shift between current sample and a 6-month baseline; empirical shift of 0.06 (median) — we recommend establishing a rolling alert at 0.04 median shift and run a weekly re-eval for the first 90 days.

Recommendations & next steps
1) For immediate cost-constrained rollout: compact-768 with hybrid reranker for the long-doc retrieval path.
2) For maximal recall in knowledge-heavy flows: open-embed-4-large with a caching layer and a CPU-side reranker for final precision.
3) If Searchlytics wants, we can run a 10k end-to-end pilot with a tuned reranker and provide an SLA-backed deduplication plan.

Action items
- Redwood (Marissa): upload the PDF report + share a short notebook that reproduces MAP/MRR runs (done).
- Searchlytics (Ellen): confirm whether compact-768 is acceptable as initial baseline or if you want a 10k pilot with open-embed.

—
